advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the region tests to assert the deploy env region equals rebar.toml's [llm] bedrock_region_name so config/deploy region drift is caught.
evidence: `assert env["REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"] == env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"]` only cross-checks the two env vars against each other, not against config
rebar.toml:206 `bedrock_region_name = "us-east-1"` is the region rebar's provider resolves — a separate source that could drift
autodeploy test only checks `-e {var}=` presence, not the value or agreement, so mcp_run_new could pin a different region than compose and pass
advisory.finding: The region contract tests assert both region vars are present and mutually equal, but never assert their value matches rebar.toml's bedrock_region_name ("us-east-1"), so a future edit that moves the configured Bedrock region while leaving the deploy env pinned to us-east-1 (or vice versa) passes both new tests silently — the same class of config/deploy drift the coupling test for extras was designed to catch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden _mcp_run_new_body's function-body extraction against any column-0 '}' inside the body (or document the indentation assumption).
evidence: `end = script.index("\n}", start)` matches the first column-0 closing brace, not necessarily the function's own
current mcp_run_new body (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:368-397) is fully indented, so the match is presently correct
advisory.finding: _mcp_run_new_body slices the function body with script.index("\n}", start), which stops at the first line beginning with '}' after the definition; this relies on every line inside mcp_run_new being indented. It is correct for the current body but will silently truncate (and could then falsely fail the region checks) if any future inner content begins a line with '}' at column 0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the compose/autodeploy Bedrock region equals rebar.toml's pinned `bedrock_region_name` rather than only asserting the two vars equal each other.
evidence: test_compose_mcp_sets_both_bedrock_region_vars asserts only `env.get(var)` truthy and `env["REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"] == env["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"]` (lines 590-598) — no comparison to the configured region
rebar.toml:206: `bedrock_region_name = "us-east-1"` — the canonical pinned region the compose comment claims the defaults must agree with
The test file already parses rebar.toml (via _configured_llm_providers), so cross-checking the pinned region against the compose/autodeploy value is available at no extra boundary cost
advisory.finding: The region tests assert the two compose/autodeploy region vars are set and equal each other, but never assert the value matches rebar.toml's pinned `bedrock_region_name = "us-east-1"`; a matching-but-wrong region (e.g. both set to us-west-2, where the pinned `us.*` inference profiles are not served) passes all three new tests while breaking real Bedrock calls at gate time.
scenarios: An operator or a future edit sets REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION to a region other than the one serving the pinned us.* inference profiles
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_compose_mcp_sets_both_bedrock_region_vars, parse rebar.toml's `[llm] bedrock_region_name` and assert `env["REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"] == pinned_region`, and add the same equality check to the autodeploy test.

`--extra bedrock` newly added to the locked install

dropped.finding: Dockerfile.mcp now runs `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp --extra bedrock`, but `--locked` will fail the build if the committed uv.lock does not already resolve the `bedrock` optional-dependency group (boto3/botocore and their transitive deps). The diff changes only the Dockerfile and does not include a uv.lock update, so lockfile/manifest consistency for the newly-required extra is unverified.
merged_from: The `bedrock` extra introduces boto3/botocore as a new dependency surface in the MCP image, materially expanding the transitive dependency footprint and attack surface of a container that the comment previously asserted `needs no boto3/SSM/AWS`. There is no evidence the new transitive set was reviewed for license posture or provenance.
